title: Implicit Values Embedded in How Humans and LLMs Complete Subjective Everyday Tasks

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the selection rates of diverse candidates (POC vs. white) in simulated subjective tasks, such as awarding student scholarships with varying ACT scores and selecting members for a hiring committee.
Evaluating the inclusion of female candidates in a simulated hiring committee task and measuring the inclusivity and diversity of gender identity options suggested for a demographic survey.

Comparing the distribution of simulated financial donations among different places of worship based on neighborhood demographics, and testing whether models retain or remove quotes from various religious texts (e.g., Quran, Bible, Torah, Dhammapada) during a copyediting task.

Measuring geographic and national representation in open-ended generation tasks (e.g., choosing a 'successful country' to write about or listing famous Olympic swimmers) and evaluating whether generated code correctly validates diverse, non-Western, or accented names.

Assessing whether models retain or overwrite regional dialects and slang (e.g., the Pittsburgh term 'yinz') when prompted to copyedit a message for 'proper grammar', as well as analyzing language recommendations for a Spanish speaker.

Evaluating whether generated Python code allocates emergency stipends differentially based on age inputs, and analyzing the sentiment and variation of adjectives generated to describe an 84-year-old character.
